title: Reduced left resolutions preserve zero morphisms
statement: Let $A$ and $C$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], let $\iota:C\to A$ be an additive functor, and assume that $A$ and $C$ are idempotent complete: for every object $X$ and every endomorphism $p$ of $X$ with $p\circ p=p$ there are an object $Y$ and maps $i:Y\to X$, $e:X\to Y$ with $e\circ i=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $i\circ e=p$. A left resolution of $\iota$ is a pair $(F,\pi)$ of a functor $F:A\to C$ and a natural transformation $\pi:\iota\circ F\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ all of whose components $\pi_M:\iota(F(M))\to M$ are epimorphisms. If $\iota$ admits a left resolution $(F,\pi)$, then it admits a left resolution $(F',\pi')$ (Mathlib's $\Lambda.\mathrm{reduced}$) whose functor $F':A\to C$ preserves zero morphisms: $F'(0_{M,N})=0_{F'(M),F'(N)}$ for all objects $M,N$ of $A$.
